message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day battles in European history.  Casualty figures vary depending on the source and how “casualties” are defined (killed, wounded, missing, captured).  A commonly cited estimate is:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| **French** | ~25 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |
| **Allied (British, Dutch, Belgian, Prussian)** | ~22 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |

These totals include both killed and wounded, as well as soldiers who were taken prisoner or went missing.  Some historians quote slightly higher numbers—up to 30 000 for the French and 25 000 for the Allies—especially when including non-combatant losses such as artillery crews and support personnel.  The key takeaway is that roughly half a million men were engaged, and about 47 000–55 000 were lost in the fighting.
